ai.title: Add generate-plan agent to base2 orchestration
ai.summary: New `generate-plan` agent added to `.agents/planners/` and integrated into `base2` orchestration, replacing `decomposing-thinker`, `independent-thinker`, `code-sketcher`, and `editor`. `base2.ts` now spawns `generate-plan` for planning, simplifying the agent layer structure. `generate-plan` uses `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` to generate 5 alternative plans, analyze them, and select the simplest optimal plan via `set_output`.

eli5.text: The assistant system now picks a single smarter helper to plan tasks instead of juggling four separate helpers. When you ask it to build something complex, one dedicated planner evaluates five different ways to tackle it and chooses the simplest strong option before the rest of the team gets to work. This streamlines how your requests are broken down internally, reducing handoffs between helpers. It is live today as part of the base orchestration layer.

ai.title: Add buffbench score analysis script and task-numbered logs
ai.summary: Added scripts/analyze-buffbench-logs.ts to aggregate and print score tables from buffbench ANALYSIS logs. Modified evals/buffbench/run-buffbench.ts to prepend task index to trace and analysis filenames for easier sorting. Updated evals/buffbench/main.ts to use base2-simple agent, increase commitConcurrency to 20, and force exit.

eli5.text: The team added a tool that can read and print score tables from buffbench log files, making it easier to review how different setups performed. They also tweaked the logging system to prepend a task number to file names, so files sort in the correct order and are easier to trace. Additionally, they adjusted the main runner to use a simplified agent, bumped the concurrency limit, and force an exit at the end. These changes streamline internal evaluation and make log analysis more practical.

ai.title: Move unused agent definitions to .agents-graveyard
ai.summary: Relocates 14 agent definitions (brainstormer, creative-catalyst, knowledge-keeper, openset/*, planners/*, reviewer/decomposing) from `.agents` to new `.agents-graveyard` directory. Updates import paths for relative references. Includes new `base2-with-context-discoverer.ts` and `context-discoverer.ts` definitions in graveyard. Internal cleanup of unused agent code.

eli5.text: The company moved 14 unused helper programs (like the brainstormer and reviewer tools) out of the active workspace into a separate 'graveyard' folder where they are kept but no longer run or affect daily operations. Anyone working on the system will see these tools have changed addresses, requiring updated connection paths, but regular users won't notice any difference since these programs were already inactive.

ai.title: Refactor agent output and message utils
ai.summary: Moved `getAgentOutput` and `buildUserMessageContent` from `run-agent-step.ts` to dedicated utility files `util/agent-output.ts` and `util/messages.ts`. This refactoring, suggested by CodeBuff, isolates logic for better maintainability. Scope limited to backend core utilities.

eli5.text: The team tidied up how the assistant's responses and conversation messages are built by moving two key pieces of logic into their own dedicated spots. If you watched the codebase, you'd see that the behind-the-scenes functions for shaping what the assistant outputs and how user messages are assembled are no longer tangled up in the main workflow file. This doesn't change what the software does for anyone, but it makes the code easier to follow and adjust later on. It's purely structural housekeeping affecting the backend system.

ai.title: Add generate-plan-max agent with 5-iteration selection
ai.summary: Introduced `generate-plan-max` agent spawning 5 `generate-plan` instances and selecting the best via `plan-selector`. Updated `agent-builder.ts` to reference new planner files and modified `plan-selector.ts` to focus on high-level plan evaluation without file reading. Internal planner subsystem only.

eli5.text: When you ask the planning assistant to come up with the best possible step-by-step plan, it no longer just tries once or twice. It now quietly generates five different draft plans at the same time, then picks the single best one before presenting it to you. So you get a plan that’s been pre-filtered from several options, rather than the first good-enough version the assistant landed on. This only affects internal planning behavior behind the scenes; nothing you see or do differently is required to get it.

ai.title: Add SSE endpoint request analytics event
ai.summary: Added `SSE_ENDPOINT_REQUEST` to `AnalyticsEvent` enum and implemented tracking in `/api/v1/chat/completions` route. Captures request body and user ID for SSE endpoint usage monitoring. Affects `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts` and `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/route.ts`.

eli5.text: The system now records when someone uses the conversational assistant through the web browser, noting who it is and what they asked for. This information is captured the moment a request is made. You wouldn't see anything different in your experience, but your usage is now being logged for monitoring purposes. The change is live today and applies to anyone using the chat feature in their browser.

ai.title: Move SSEENDPOINTREQUEST to api analytics category
ai.summary: Analytics enum `SSE_ENDPOINT_REQUEST` moves from Web to new API category. String value updates `web.sse_endpoint_request` to `api.sse_endpoint_request`. Affects `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`. Existing dashboards filtering by `web.sse_endpoint_request` need query updates.

eli5.text: The way the system records when someone asks for a live data feed from the app has quietly changed: those events used to be filed under the 'web' section of reports, and they are now filed under the 'api' section instead. If you use a dashboard or report that looks for the old 'web' name, it will stop seeing this activity until the report is pointed at the new 'api' name. No behavior in the product itself changed, it’s just how the system labels and tracks that action for metrics. This is already live today.

ai.title: Fix context pruner instructions prompt in base
ai.summary: Removed injected instructions prompt from base context in .agents/context-pruner.ts. Current messages array now pops the final element before token counting. Test coverage updated in .agents/__tests__/context-pruner.test.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant is trimming down a long conversation to fit within its memory limit, it now removes the last message in the conversation before it starts counting, specifically the message that contains hidden setup instructions that were injected at the very end. This means those internal instructions will no longer accidentally count against the memory budget, giving slightly more room to what you've actually typed. You won't see this directly, but in long conversations the assistant may trim or summarize your content a touch less aggressively than before, because it's no longer wasting its token budget on its own internal setup prompts. This is an internal maintenance tweak with no visible change to your experience, and it is live today.

ai.title: Refactor BuffBench evals and Base2 agent definition
ai.summary: Renamed `commitConcurrency` to `taskConcurrency` in `runBuffBench` options and removed manual result writing from `main.ts`. Updated `createBase2` in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` to return `Omit<SecretAgentDefinition, 'id'>`, moving `id` assignment to the export site. This clarifies agent definition construction and standardizes eval concurrency naming.

eli5.text: The engineers renamed a setting that controls how many tasks run at once during internal testing from 'commitConcurrency' to 'taskConcurrency' so it better describes what it does. They also moved where each AI assistant in the testing system gets its unique name, so the name is now assigned only when the assistant is actually used rather than inside the setup function. These are behind-the-scenes changes to keep the testing system organized and easier to maintain. You wouldn't notice any difference in how the system performs.

ai.summary: generate-plan-thinking agent moved to .agents-graveyard/planners. Agent spawned decomposing-thinker and independent-thinker to generate five alternative plans, then selected the optimal one via set_output. Internal change only; no user-facing surfaces affected.

eli5.text: The team retired an older planning agent, moving it into an archive section of the project where unused pieces are stored. This means that specific tool, which was designed to generate and evaluate multiple plans before choosing the best one, is no longer active or in use. If you went looking for it, you would find it set aside among other retired components rather than running like the current tools do. This is an internal change, so it does not affect anything visible to you today.

ai.title: Reviewer prompt injects original user request
ai.summary: The reviewer agent definition in `.agents/reviewer/reviewer.ts` now includes the original user prompt via `PLACEHOLDER.USER_INPUT_PROMPT`. This change addresses a gap where the reviewer lacked context on the initial request, ensuring feedback aligns with user intent. The `instructionsPrompt` was updated to wrap this input in `<user_message>` tags and added a directive to verify all user requirements are met. Internal change to agent prompt structure.

eli5.text: The assistant's built-in reviewer now reads your original request before it checks the changes the assistant made. Previously, the reviewer only saw the final code edits and could miss whether they actually matched what you first asked for. Now the request is shown to the reviewer so it can flag anything that drifted from your original intent. This went live today.

ai.title: Inject requestToolCall dependency into agent runtime
ai.summary: Refactored tool execution to inject `requestToolCall` as a dependency rather than importing it directly from `websocket-action`. Added `backend/src/client-wrapper.ts` implementing `requestToolCallWs` with timeout handling and WebSocket subscription logic. Updated `main-prompt.ts`, `tool-executor.ts`, and `batch-str-replace.ts` to accept `RequestToolCallFn` via `AgentRuntimeScopedDeps` types. This decouples core agent logic from specific WebSocket transport implementations, facilitating testability and alternative client bindings.

eli5.text: The software's helper tools used to be hardcoded to talk to one specific communication system, so swapping out how the assistant talks to the outside world required rewriting core files. Now those tools receive that communication method as a parameter instead, like handing someone a phone rather than bolting a specific phone line into their desk. You won't see a new button or setting, but the system is now structured so developers can plug in different ways for the assistant to receive data and send results, including ones that fail faster if something stalls. This is a behind-the-scenes change that affects only people editing the program's internals today.

ai.title: Inject requestMcpToolData dependency into Agent Runtime
ai.summary: Backend refactors MCP tool data fetching to use dependency injection via `requestMcpToolData` in `AgentRuntimeScopedDeps` instead of direct WebSocket coupling. `getMCPToolData` in `backend/src/mcp/util.ts` now accepts the injected function, removing the `ws` parameter. `backend/src/client-wrapper.ts` implements `requestMcpToolDataWs` for production, while `common/src/testing/impl/agent-runtime.ts` provides a test stub. This decouples MCP logic from transport details for better testability.

eli5.text: The backend now passes the tool-fetching capability around to other parts of the system instead of each part grabbing the live data connection directly, which is a behind-the-scenes code cleanup that makes it easier to test how the assistant handles external tools. You won't see any new behavior today since this just reorganizes how things connect; the assistant still fetches and uses tools the same way it did before.

ai.title: Inject requestFiles and requestOptionalFile into tool handlers
ai.summary: Refactors backend tool handlers to accept `requestFiles` and `requestOptionalFile` functions as injected dependencies rather than importing them directly. This decouples `str-replace`, `read-files`, and `find-files` from specific WebSocket implementations, allowing `getFileReadingUpdates` and related utilities to operate via passed-in parameters. Scope covers `backend/src/client-wrapper.ts` (new WS helpers), `backend/src/get-file-reading-updates.ts`, and multiple tool handlers in `backend/src/tools/`. `requestFilesWs` now ensures file contents end with a newline via `ensureEndsWithNewline` before returning.

eli5.text: The way the system asks for and receives files from the app has been reorganized so that the file-reading tools no longer depend on a single, hardcoded connection method. Instead, the tools that search and display file contents now receive the file-fetching helper from whoever is running them, letting those tools work through different connection styles without changing their own code. The reorganized file-fetching now also guarantees each returned file ends with a blank line, keeping file contents consistent. Existing tests for the tool behaviors remain in place and continue to pass under the new structure.

ai.title: Remove unused WebSocket type from backend agent steps
ai.summary: Removed unused `WebSocket` type imports and parameters from `main-prompt.ts`, `run-agent-step.ts`, `batch-str-replace.ts`, and `find-files.ts`. Eliminates dead code paths and simplifies function signatures by dropping the `ws` dependency where it was never utilized. Internal refactor; no user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The assistant's behind-the-scenes plumbing got tidied up: a piece of data called a WebSocket connection, which was being passed around in the system like an empty cable, has been unplugged wherever it was going unused. The software behaves exactly as before; users won't notice a difference, but the code is now simpler and lighter for whoever has to maintain it.
